module

public import Mathlib.Order.Nat

public section

namespace Nat
variable {p : ℕ → Prop} [DecidablePred p] {n : ℕ}

lemma find_of_isLeast (hn : IsLeast {n | p n} n) : Nat.find (p := p) ⟨n, hn.1⟩ = n := by
  rw [find_eq_iff]; exact ⟨hn.1, fun m hmn hm ↦ hmn.not_ge <| hn.2 hm⟩

end Nat

review.notes:
The file contains only Nat.find_of_isLeast and introduces no definitions. Its statement correctly identifies Nat.find with a supplied least element. IsLeast includes membership, so its hypothesis supplies genuine existence and excludes the empty-predicate case. The particular existence proof passed to Nat.find does not change its value. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean I proved Nat.find hp = n ↔ IsLeast {k | p k} n for arbitrary hp, verified the usual minimum characterization, and tested empty, zero, singleton, positive, and multiple-witness cases. The lemma has no sorryAx dependency. Both scratch files compile without errors or warnings.

The sole use, OeisA108129.a_of_isLeast, agrees with OEIS A108129's minimum exponent m ≥ 1. /workspace/review/use_site.lean verifies its minimum characterization for n ≠ 0 and the boundary cases. OEIS has offset 1, so the extension a 0 = 0 does not affect the conjecture. Direct OEIS requests were blocked; the entry was read through OEIS's data mirror. The linked Riesel reference, updated July 29, 2026, still records the conjecture as open. No repository files were edited.
